sample_unit: scored evaluations (110 pharmacogenomic cases, nine LLMs)
models_evaluated: nine frontier large language models (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Lethal-class pharmacogenomic errors with and without retrieval grounding in guidelines
links.effect: Retrieval raised phenotype accuracy but paradoxically increased lethal-class errors; versioned skills executed as code did not increase them. No numbers given in the abstract.
links.quote: Letting the model reason was stochastic and unsafe, and grounding it in the correct guidelines by retrieval paradoxically increased lethal-class errors.

links.outcome: LLM interpretation of real star-allele diplotypes across ancestry groups
links.effect: Unguarded model interpretation degraded along an ancestry gradient across European, Latin American and East African populations (>7,000 individuals); executed mapping was population-invariant.
links.quote: On individual genomes, unguarded model interpretation degraded along an ancestry gradient; execution removes this gradient from the clinical mapping, relocating it to the auditable completeness of the input caller.

links.outcome: Stochasticity and safety of unconstrained model reasoning on pharmacogenomic cases
links.effect: Letting the model reason was stochastic and unsafe; executing the skill made the mapping deterministic and identical across models.
links.quote: Letting the model reason was stochastic and unsafe, and grounding it in the correct guidelines by retrieval paradoxically increased lethal-class errors.

unlisted_practices: Encoding validated decision logic as a versioned skill executed as deterministic code, with the LLM confined to input interpretation
Using a deterministic input caller and abstaining on the irreducible residual

screen.practice: retrieval grounding vs executing validated decision logic as versioned code skill
screen.reason: Empirically tests and compares safety/error rates across different pipeline architectures and guardrails (pure reasoning vs. retrieval grounding vs. code-executed versioned skills) for agentic LLMs in pharmacogenomics.

primary.practice: versioned skill library execution and retrieval-augmented grounding guardrails
